title: A digital clock
description:
Read a number of seconds from 0 to 86399 (one day) with `read_int`, and print it as a 24-hour clock time with two digits for each part, followed by a new line:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `3725` | `01:02:05` |
| `0` | `00:00:00` |
| `86399` | `23:59:59` |

Do **not** use `print_int` or `print_uint`: work out each digit with `div`, add `'0'`, store the eight characters and the new line into a buffer in `.bss`, and print them with one `write` system call.

Hours are seconds ÷ 3600; what is left, ÷ 60, gives the minutes; the remainder is the seconds. Each two-digit part is (part ÷ 10) and (part remainder 10).

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .bss
clock:  resb    9

        section .text
_start:
        call    read_int

        mov     byte [rel clock], '0'
        mov     byte [rel clock + 1], 10
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel clock]
        mov     edx, 2
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .bss
clock:  resb    9

        section .text
_start:
        call    read_int                ; rax = seconds
        xor     edx, edx
        mov     ecx, 3600
        div     ecx                     ; eax = hours, edx = the rest
        mov     ebx, edx                ; keep the rest

        xor     edx, edx
        mov     ecx, 10
        div     ecx                     ; eax = tens of hours, edx = units
        add     al, '0'
        mov     [rel clock], al
        add     dl, '0'
        mov     [rel clock + 1], dl
        mov     byte [rel clock + 2], ':'

        mov     eax, ebx
        xor     edx, edx
        mov     ecx, 60
        div     ecx                     ; eax = minutes, edx = seconds
        mov     ebx, edx

        xor     edx, edx
        mov     ecx, 10
        div     ecx
        add     al, '0'
        mov     [rel clock + 3], al
        add     dl, '0'
        mov     [rel clock + 4], dl
        mov     byte [rel clock + 5], ':'

        mov     eax, ebx
        xor     edx, edx
        div     ecx                     ; ecx is still 10
        add     al, '0'
        mov     [rel clock + 6], al
        add     dl, '0'
        mov     [rel clock + 7], dl
        mov     byte [rel clock + 8], 10

        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel clock]
        mov     edx, 9
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `div` divides `rdx:rax` by its operand: put the number in `rax`, zero `rdx`, and after `div rcx` the quotient is in `rax` and the remainder in `rdx`.
Work out hours, minutes and seconds first; then split each into tens (`÷ 10`) and units (`mod 10`), add `'0'` to each, and store them with the colons and the new line into your 9-byte buffer.
rules: Work out the digits yourself instead of print_int.
Use div to split the time.
